But that it may live, perhaps the dignity of the subject matter will bring it about, and likewise the authority of the Bard whom I have plundered: for nothing has flowed from the rich vein of Maro that is not worthy of eternal memory. prose.la: Lector quisquis es, siste, in hoc limine paulisper te moror. Quod hîc damus, sacrum est, de spoliis profanorum. Dederunt ipsum ante me multi, sed à se, suisque verbis: ego sic malui alienis. Phrygium efformamus aulæum, pretiosis & variis aliorum telis, viliora rudis ingenij nostri fila interteximus, ne dissutum opus vndique diffluat. Centonem si dixeris, non penitus aberrabis; in quo mirari desine tam nostraesse omnia, quàm ferè nihil. A nobis sunt inuentio, & rerum ordo; versus, & hemistichia hausimus è Virgilio pleraque, hoc est, ex ipso fonte ornatæ Poëseos. Ac ne, quod aiunt, arenam sine calce afferremus, sparsas Poëtæ principis sententias, iam inter se commodè vinximus, iam verborum nostrorum quodam velut cæmento commisimus. Non poterit homini id ætatis vitio verti, cùm multa dixerit, à se pauca locutum esse: iam enim eorum in albo sum, quibus
prose.en: Reader, whoever you are, halt; I delay you for a little while on this threshold. What we offer here is sacred, from the spoils of the profane. Many have offered the same before me, but from themselves, and in their own words: I have thus preferred to do so in the words of others. We are fashioning a Phrygian tapestry; into the precious and varied webs of others, we have interwoven the cheaper threads of our own unpolished intellect, lest the unstitched work fall apart on all sides. If you call it a cento, you will not be entirely wrong; in which cease to wonder that everything is as much ours as almost nothing is. From us come the invention and the order of things; the verses and half-lines we have mostly drawn from Virgil, that is, from the very fountain of ornate poetry. And lest, as they say, we should bring sand without lime, we have at times conveniently bound together the scattered thoughts of the prince of poets, at times joined them with a sort of cement, as it were, of our own words. It cannot be turned into a fault for a man of that age, though he has said many things, to have spoken few from himself: for I am already on the register of those, to whom

prose.la: Suum enim singulis corymbion fideliter remitto, contentus elegantiæ Virgilianæ, Christianæ fidei, pietatisque solidæ nectar affudisse; vt in ea, velut in artificioso Mentoris scypho, cum literarum ornatu veræ succum religionis inueniat & hauriat Iuuentus studiosa. Quàm nihil sit hoc præstitisse, post intermissa nouem lustris literarum studia, tu dispice. Quamquam enim suaue sit Pimplæis fontibus vuescere, tamen vbi iam annorum frequentia, earum, quæ prima inhæserant iuuentute, rerum obliuionem inuexit, labor hic, vel te iudice,
prose.en: For I faithfully return to each his own hairpiece, content to have poured the nectar of Christian faith and solid piety upon Virgilian elegance; so that in it, as in an artfully crafted cup of Mentor, studious Youth may find and drink the essence of true religion along with the ornament of letters. Consider for yourself how trifling a thing it is to have accomplished this, after literary studies had been interrupted for nine lustres. For although it is sweet to be moistened by the Pimplean springs, nevertheless when the multitude of years has already brought on a forgetfulness of those things which had taken root in early youth, this labor, even in your judgment,

prose.la: Sed amaritudinem hanc detersit planè, quem inde spero, fructus. Nonne enim magnum videri debet, si quæ fidei documenta, soluto sermone, Christiana Iuuentus semel imbiberit, velut saluti necessaria, ea tanti Poëtæ expressa versibus, altiùs inhæreant? Fruere, Lector, & emarcidi iam trunci malum insititium, explicata fronte deliba.
prose.en: But the fruit which I hope for from it has completely wiped away this bitterness. For ought it not to seem a great thing, if those teachings of the faith which Christian Youth has once imbibed in prose, as necessary for salvation, should take deeper root when expressed in the verses of so great a Poet? Enjoy, Reader, and with an unfurrowed brow taste the grafted fruit of a trunk now withered.

prose.en: Since four theologians of our Society, to whom this was entrusted, have examined the Maronian Catholic Muse of the Reverend Father Aegidius Bavarius, and have approved that it may be published, by the power granted to me by our Very Reverend Father Mutius Vitelleschi, Superior General of our Society, I grant to Martinus Nutius, printer of Antwerp, permission to print it. In witness whereof I have issued these letters, signed with my own hand and sealed with the seal of my office, at Antwerp, October 15, in the year 1621.

printed_notes.text_en: A description of the Muse of Maro.
printed_notes.explanation: This note labels the portrait that follows. Virgil’s Muse—once the source of Mantua’s pagan poetic glory—is imagined as cleansed by the river of life, worshipping God, and offering honour at Christian altars: a miniature statement of the book’s conversion of Virgil to Catholic use.

printed_notes.text: Docemur hîc, dum in dubio est animus, vt in fide Catholica roboremur, non esse vllo modo ad vanas superstitiones recurrendum, sed crebra frequentique oratione, variáque corporis maceratione ad Christum Dominum serio confugiendum, offerendo ei sacrificium. Agni immaculati, & cæsarum ouium, sanctorum Martyrum: gestando cilicium, in pellibus caprinis, in melotis noctes ducendo insomnes, vt possimus à Deo visitari, eiusque diuino lumine illustrari.
printed_notes.text_en: We are taught here that, while the mind is in doubt, so that we may be strengthened in the Catholic faith, we must in no way resort to vain superstitions, but rather earnestly take refuge in Christ the Lord through frequent and repeated prayer, and various mortifications of the body, offering to him the sacrifice of the immaculate Lamb, and of the slaughtered sheep, the holy Martyrs: wearing a hairshirt, spending sleepless nights in goatskins and sheepskins, so that we may be visited by God, and illuminated by his divine light.
printed_notes.explanation: Bavarius rejects pagan divination in the preceding Virgilian lines and supplies a Catholic alternative: prayer, ascetic discipline, Christ’s sacrifice, the martyrs, and monastic penitential dress.

printed_notes.text_en: a The Romans are by the best right called lords of the world, because in the possession of the Roman and Apostolic Church herself are all the spiritual treasures of the Christian religion. b Christ the Lord wished to give us wine in the sacrifice of the Mass, which brings forth virgins.
printed_notes.explanation: The note converts Virgil’s imperial Rome into the Roman Church and its treasury of spiritual authority.

printed_notes.text: Saltibus in vacuis ieiunij & abstinentiæ, inueniunt oues Christi pinguia pascua: iisdem sunt plena flumina aquæ salientis in vitam aternam, de fontibus Saluatoris. Hic muscum intelligo alterius generis, quàm sit is qui vel è terra, vel ab animantibus producitur, sed inodorem suauitatis, à fama boni nominis procedit. Viridissima gramine ripa, est repagulum castitatis. Speluncæq; tegant Monachos & Anachoretas, sub umbra alarum Christi Domini, qua ob defensionis robur, saxea dici potest. Per canes, & Spartæ catulos acremque molossum concionatores intellige, quos sero pingui sacræ doctrinæ, à Sede Apostolica conuenit imbui, vt alios doceant, quæ prosint ad salutem.
printed_notes.text_en: In the empty glades of fasting and abstinence, the sheep of Christ find rich pastures; there too the rivers are full of water springing up into eternal life, from the fountains of the Saviour. Here by 'muscus' I understand something of another kind than that which is produced either from the earth or from animals: rather, an odor of sweetness, which proceeds from the fame of a good name. The bank greenest with grass is the barrier of chastity. And let caves shelter Monks and Anchorites under the shadow of the wings of Christ the Lord, which, because of the strength of its defense, may be called rocky. By the dogs, the whelps of Sparta, and the fierce Molossian, understand preachers, who ought to be steeped by the Apostolic See in the rich whey of sacred doctrine, so that they may teach others what is profitable for salvation.
printed_notes.explanation: Bavarius allegorizes Virgil’s pastoral landscape as Christian ascetic life. Pasture and water become spiritual nourishment; caves shelter monks; fragrance signifies reputation; and Virgil’s dogs become preachers trained in Catholic doctrine under the authority of the Apostolic See.

printed_notes.text: Indulgendum putaui neophytae Musae Maronis, vt ad singula Dei praecepta, gentis suae profana citet exempla,cum huius instituti mei ratio postulet, vt eum more suo loquentem,quoad eius fieri possit,audiamus.
printed_notes.text_en: I thought indulgence should be granted to the neophyte Muse of Maro, so that at each of God's commandments she might cite profane examples of her own race, since the rationale of this my design demands that we hear him speaking in his own manner, as far as it can be done.
printed_notes.explanation: Bavarius licenses his novice Muse to use pagan examples under each commandment because speaking in Maro’s own idiom is part of the cento’s declared method.

printed_notes.text: Conceditur liberis matrimonium, non præcipitur. Nam, vt ait Apostolus 1. Cor. 7. Melius est nubere, quàm vri. Seruanda verò ab iis castitas, qui se huic voto astrinxerunt.
printed_notes.text_en: Marriage is permitted to the free, not commanded. For, as the Apostle says in 1 Cor. 7: It is better to marry than to burn. But chastity must be kept by those who have bound themselves to this vow.
printed_notes.explanation: The note distinguishes marriage as a permission from celibacy as a binding religious vow and cites 1 Corinthians 7:9.

printed_notes.text: Hoc intelligendum est non quouis die ieiunij, sed tantùm in Quadragesima, quo tempore vsus ouorum in diem Paschæ prohibetur.

printed_notes.explanation: The gloss limits the preceding dietary image to the stricter Lenten fast and specifies the contemporary rule about eggs.

printed_notes.text: Dulce frenum confessio, sensualitati refrenandæ commodum, quo a peccando abducatur.
printed_notes.text_en: Confession is a sweet bridle, suitable for restraining sensuality, by which one may be led away from sinning.
printed_notes.explanation: The note makes Virgil’s bridle an allegory of confession’s discipline of desire.

printed_notes.text: Si peccati mortalis culpa teneatur, prout etiam inferiori ætate, grauioris peccati conscij esse possumus, teste S. Greg. in suis Dialogis.
printed_notes.text_en: If one is held by the guilt of mortal sin, just as even at a younger age we can be conscious of a graver sin, as St. Gregory witnesses in his Dialogues.
printed_notes.explanation: This qualifies the preceding age rule: grave sin can create an obligation to confess even before the usual age.

printed_notes.text: Ne cui difficile sit conscientiam examinare, huic suam sacerdos opem in peccatis eruendis pollicetur.
printed_notes.text_en: Lest it be difficult for anyone to examine his conscience, the priest promises him his help in drawing out sins.
printed_notes.explanation: The priest assists the penitent’s examination of conscience; the gloss explains the agricultural image of turning over hidden soil.

printed_notes.text: Designatur hic Sacrosanctum Eucharistiæ Sacramentum, prout in re diuina sumitur.
printed_notes.text_en: Here is designated the Most Holy Sacrament of the Eucharist, as it is received in the divine service.
printed_notes.explanation: The first banquet image is identified specifically with reception of the Eucharist at Mass.

printed_notes.text_en: The table of communion is destined for the great supper.
printed_notes.explanation: The banquet table becomes the Eucharistic communion table.

printed_notes.text: Dant famuli lymphas in Missæ sacrificio.
printed_notes.text_en: The servants give water in the sacrifice of the Mass.
printed_notes.explanation: Virgil’s serving attendants and water are mapped onto the liturgical service of the Mass.

lines.en: First of all, at the rising of the light we are brought forth into the breezes.

lines.en: to be strengthened on all sides with gathered strength,

lines.en: to grow, and to be increased until firm bones and muscles

printed_notes.text: Designantur per lupos hæresiarchæ, qui Sacramenta Ecclesiæ contemnunt atque repudiant.
printed_notes.text_en: By the wolves are designated the heresiarchs, who despise and repudiate the Sacraments of the Church.
printed_notes.explanation: Virgil’s wolves are identified with leaders of heresy who reject Catholic sacramental life.

printed_notes.text: Hæc allegoricè intelligenda sunt de refrigeriis ouium Christi, quibus hæretici, prout de numero istarum ouium non sunt, verum lupi rapaces, iusto Dei iudicio, omnino destituuntur.
printed_notes.text_en: These things are to be understood allegorically concerning the refreshments of the sheep of Christ, of which heretics, since they are not of the number of those sheep, but rather ravenous wolves, by the just judgment of God, are entirely deprived.
printed_notes.explanation: The pastoral refreshment is sacramental grace, reserved for Christ’s flock and denied to the predatory wolves.

printed_notes.text_en: We are born.
We are strengthened.
We are nourished.
We need medicine.
We are restored.

printed_notes.text: Primò designantur hæretici, qui sacrosanctum hoc Sacramentum sacrilegis manibus profanoque ore & corde violant.
printed_notes.text_en: First are designated the heretics, who violate this sacrosanct Sacrament with sacrilegious hands and with profane mouth and heart.
printed_notes.explanation: The first group profanes the Eucharist through doctrinal rejection and sacrilegious reception.

printed_notes.text: Secundi generis sunt illi, qui ex necessitate, ac metu mortis dumtaxat communicant.
printed_notes.text_en: Of the second kind are those who communicate only out of necessity and fear of death.
printed_notes.explanation: The second group approaches the sacrament only under the pressure of danger or death.

printed_notes.text: Notantur frigidi Catholici, qui nisi lege tenerentur, vix semel in anno ad sanctam hanc mensam accederent.
printed_notes.text_en: Noted are the cold Catholics, who, were they not bound by law, would scarcely approach this holy table once a year.
printed_notes.explanation: The third group complies only with the minimum annual Easter-communion obligation.

printed_notes.text: Per tribulas, trahas, rastra dentibus armata, quibus terra pungitur & conteritur, insinuandam duxi cordis nostri compunctionem, vt est prima pars pœnitentiæ. Per aratrum verò, & vomerem, quo terra aperitur, euertitur, & quasi euomitur, confessionem ipsam, quæ est secunda pars eiusdem Sacramenti, non incongruè intelligendam putaui, quatenus ipsa confessione nostram conscientiam Christi vicario aperimus, & sordes animi eruimus. Per mysticam denique vannum, qua purgatur frumentum, & à palea secernitur, vti etiam per tarda Eleusinæ matris voluentia plaustra, quibus seges in horreum inuehitur, satisfactionem intelligo, qua mouemur ad faciendos fructus dignos pœnitentiæ. Luc. 3.
printed_notes.text_en: By the threshing-sledges, drags, and harrows armed with teeth, by which the earth is pricked and crushed, I considered that the compunction of our heart should be suggested, as it is the first part of penance. But by the plough, and the ploughshare, by which the earth is opened, turned over, and as it were vomited out, I thought that confession itself, which is the second part of the same Sacrament, should not incongruously be understood, insofar as by confession itself we open our conscience to the vicar of Christ, and root out the filth of the soul. Finally, by the mystic winnowing fan, by which the grain is purged and separated from the chaff, as also by the slow-rolling wagons of the Eleusinian mother, by which the crop is carried into the barn, I understand satisfaction, by which we are moved to produce fruits worthy of penance. Luke 3.
printed_notes.explanation: The entire farming sequence is an explicit three-part allegory of the sacrament of penance: harrowing is contrition, ploughing is confession, and winnowing and carting the crop are satisfaction.

printed_notes.text: Semina laudis opima, sunt charitas Dei & proximi, radix bonorum operum.
printed_notes.text_en: The rich seeds of praise are the love of God and of neighbour, the root of good works.
printed_notes.explanation: The first agricultural image signifies charity as the source of morally good action.

printed_notes.text: Tenues viciæ, tristesque lupini, sunt opera moraliter bona.
printed_notes.text_en: The slender vetches and bitter lupines are morally good works.
printed_notes.explanation: The modest crops represent naturally good moral acts.

printed_notes.text: Lappæ, tribulique, sunt opera mala & noxia.
printed_notes.text_en: The burrs and caltrops are evil and harmful works.
printed_notes.explanation: The harmful weeds complete the moral taxonomy by representing sinful acts.

printed_notes.text: Musa Maronis, circa octauam Beatitudinem, suam ignorantiam agnoscit, cupitque à suo Ductore, etiamsi proprio Marte vti debeat, exactius institui.
printed_notes.text_en: The Muse of Maro, concerning the eighth Beatitude, acknowledges her ignorance, and desires to be more exactly instructed by her Guide, even if he must use his own effort.
printed_notes.explanation: The note explains the dramatic handover: the Muse admits that Virgil supplies no ready doctrinal answer and asks the catechetical speaker for instruction before composing more freely in her own words.

lines.en: I shall unfold, and, duly honoured, grant favourable courses.

lines.la: Hæc sunt quæ nostra liceat te voce moneri:
lines.en: These are the things of which you may be warned by my voice:

loci.virgil: Haec sunt, quae nostra liceat te voce moneri.

lines.la: Perge modò, & qua te ducit via, dirige gressum;
lines.en: Only proceed, and where the way leads you, direct your step;

loci.virgil: Perge modo, et, qua te ducit via, dirige gressum."

lines.la: Hac etenim puppesque tuæ, pubesque tuorum,
lines.en: For by this way both your ships and the youth of your people,

loci.virgil: haud aliter puppesque tuae pubesque tuorum

lines.la: Aut portum tenet, aut pleno subit ostia velo.
lines.en: Either hold the harbour, or enter the mouth under full sail.

loci.virgil: aut portum tenet aut pleno subit ostia velo.

lines.la: MVSA.
lines.en: MUSE.

lines.la: Stat monitis parere tuis, mihi certa voluntas,
lines.en: It stands fixed to obey your warnings, my will is certain,

loci.virgil: devenient; adero, et, tua si mihi certa voluntas,

lines.la: Magna Dei genitrix, mihi iussa capessere fas est,
lines.en: Great Mother of God, for me it is right to carry out your commands,

loci.virgil: explorare labor; mihi iussa capessere fas est.

lines.la: Quo tandem detur dextræ coniungere dextram,
lines.en: So that at last it may be granted to join right hand with right hand,

loci.virgil: compellare virum et dextrae coniungere dextram.

lines.la: Ac Superûm faustas audire ac reddere voces.
lines.en: And to hear and return the auspicious voices of those above.

lines.la: O fortunati, quorum illic mænia surgunt:
lines.en: O fortunate ones, whose walls rise there:

loci.virgil: "O fortunati, quorum iam moenia surgunt!"

lines.la: Conditio at melior, quibus est fortuna peracta
lines.en: But better is the lot of those whose fortune is accomplished

loci.virgil: "Vivite felices, quibus est fortuna peracta

lines.la: Iam sua. Nos alia ex aliis in fata vocamur:
lines.en: Already as their own. We are called from one fate to another:

loci.virgil: iam sua; nos alia ex aliis in fata vocamur.

lines.la: Illis parta quies, nullum maris æquor arandum;
lines.en: For them rest is won, no expanse of sea to be ploughed;

loci.virgil: Vobis parta quies; nullum maris aequor arandum,

lines.la: Arua neque Elysij semper cedentia retro
lines.en: Nor fields of Elysium, ever receding backward,

loci.virgil: arva neque Ausoniae semper cedentia retro

lines.la: Quærenda. Interea felix, bis terque beatus,
lines.en: To be sought. Meanwhile happy, twice and thrice blessed,

lines.la: Qui simul istius fastigia suspicit vrbis,
lines.en: Is he who, as soon as he looks up at the heights of that city,

loci.virgil: Aeneas ait, et fastigia suspicit urbis.

lines.la: Acceleratque viam, gressumque ad mænia tendit;
lines.en: Both hastens his way, and directs his step toward the walls;

lines.la: Quem Deus obscuro gradientem tegmine sepsit,
lines.en: Whom, as he walks, God has fenced about with a dark covering,

lines.la: Et multo nebulæ circumdans fudit amictu,
lines.en: And, surrounding him, has poured a thick mantle of cloud over him,

loci.virgil: et multo nebulae circum dea fudit amictu,

lines.la: Cernere ne quis eum, nec quis contingere possit,
lines.en: So that no one may be able to see him, nor anyone to touch him,

loci.virgil: cernere ne quis eos, neu quis contingere posset,

printed_notes.text: * Per dexteram tellurem, viam mandatorū Dei intellige, quæ ducit ad vitam æternam.
printed_notes.text_en: * By the land on the right, understand the way of God's commandments, which leads to eternal life.
printed_notes.explanation: The right-hand route in the Virgilian landscape is the obedient path to salvation.

printed_notes.text: Per læuum latus, via perditionis insinuatur, quæ consistit in transgressione legis diuinæ.
printed_notes.text_en: By the left side is signified the way of perdition, which consists in the transgression of the divine law.
printed_notes.explanation: The left-hand route is the contrary path of disobedience and damnation.

lines.la: Moliriúe moram, aut veniendi poscere causas.
lines.en: Or to contrive a delay, or to ask the reasons for coming.

loci.virgil: molirive moram, aut veniendi poscere causas.

lines.la: Infer me precor hac nebula Deus optime septam,
lines.en: Bring me in, I pray, O God most good, enclosed in this cloud,

lines.la: Vt nisi diuinum maneat mihi mente repostum;
lines.en: So that nothing but the divine may remain stored up in my mind;

lines.la: Namque animus meminisse horret genus omne profanum:
lines.en: For my mind shudders to remember every profane kind:

loci.virgil: quamquam animus meminisse horret, luctuque refugit,

lines.la: Vna Dei subeat cari genitoris imago,
lines.en: Let the one image of God the dear Father come to mind,

loci.virgil: Obstipui; subiit cari genitoris imago,

lines.la: Vnius & Christi crudelia fata reuoluam;
lines.en: And may I ponder the cruel fates of Christ alone;

lines.la: Multa viri virtus animo, multusque recurset
lines.en: May the great virtue of the man recur to my mind, and the great

loci.virgil: Multa viri virtus animo, multusque recursat

lines.la: Laudis honos, sedeant infixi pectore vultus,
lines.en: Honor of his praise; may his features remain fixed in my breast,

lines.la: Is mihi vita, salus, dux vitæ, vera salutis
lines.en: He to me life, salvation, guide of life, the true of salvation

lines.la: Semita sit; posthac nil me mortalia tangant,
lines.en: Path let him be; hereafter let mortal things touch me not at all,

lines.la: Sitque mori lucrum cælestia regna tuenti.
lines.en: and let death be gain to one who gazes on the heavenly kingdoms.

lines.la: Iam pridem mundo effœta, vt quid inutilis annos
lines.en: Long since worn out for the world, why do I, useless, the years

lines.la: Demoror? Ah patrio tuta vt modò limine sistar.
lines.en: Delay? Ah, if only I might stand safe on my Father's threshold.

lines.la: Sit labor extremus, longarum hæc meta viarum.
lines.en: Let this be the final labor, this the goal of long journeys.

loci.virgil: Hic labor extremus, longarum haec meta viarum.

lines.la: En nos immensum spatiis confecimus æquor,
lines.en: Behold, we have completed a plain immense in its distances,

loci.virgil: Sed nos inmensum spatiis confecimus aequor,

lines.la: Et iam tempus equûm fumantia soluere colla;
lines.en: And now it is time to unyoke the smoking necks of the horses;

loci.virgil: et iam tempus equum fumantia solvere colla.

lines.la: * Hinc nos digressos faustis Deus applicet oris.
lines.en: * May God bring us, who departed from here, to auspicious shores.

printed_notes.text_en: * Through the fall of the first parents.
printed_notes.explanation: The fall described in the verse is explicitly identified with the Fall of Adam and Eve.

lines.la: ORATIO:
lines.en: PRAYER:

lines.la: ANIMA CHRISTI SANCTIFICA ME.
lines.en: SOUL OF CHRIST, SANCTIFY ME.

lines.la: Mens Christi instaurans animas, collapsaque corda,
lines.en: Mind of Christ, restoring souls and fallen hearts,

lines.la: Pectoris accelera lapsi sarcire ruinas,
lines.en: make haste to repair the ruins of my fallen breast,

loci.virgil: incumbent generis lapsi sarcire ruinas

lines.la: Numine me complens, vacuum per inane vagantem,
lines.en: filling me with your divine presence as I wander through the empty void,

lines.la: Excolar Astræa, & reliquo virtutis amictu:
lines.en: may I be adorned with Astraea and the rest of virtue's garment,

lines.la: Cùm sese agglomerent summi decora alta Parentis.
lines.en: since the lofty glories of the supreme Father gather themselves together.

lines.la: CORPVS CHRISTI SALVA ME.
lines.en: BODY OF CHRIST, SAVE ME.

lines.la: Teter abundauit cordis liquor, omniaque in se
lines.en: The foul fluid of the heart has overflowed, and all

lines.la: Ossa minutatim morbo quassata trahuntur;
lines.en: the bones, shaken by disease, are little by little drawn in upon themselves;

loci.virgil: ossa minutatim morbo collapsa trahebat.

lines.la: Quin furit, atque intus de pascitur arida febris
lines.en: Nay, a parching fever rages and feeds within upon

loci.virgil: cum furit atque artus depascitur arida febris,

lines.la: Viscera tosta siti: varius dolor occupat artus.
lines.en: the entrails scorched with thirst: manifold pain seizes the limbs.

lines.la: Quid reliqui est? medicas sectabor Apollinis artes
lines.en: What is left? Shall I pursue the healing arts of Apollo?

lines.la: Is ferat artis opem? Nihil hunc tentasse iuuabit.
lines.en: Should he bring the help of his art? It will avail nothing to have tried him.

lines.la: Sit medicans tua, Christe, caro mihi causa salutis.
lines.en: Let your healing flesh, O Christ, be the cause of my salvation.

lines.la: SANGVIS CHRISTI INEBRIA ME.
lines.en: BLOOD OF CHRIST, INEBRIATE ME.

lines.la: Congressus peto, Christe, tuos & amœna tuorum.
lines.en: I seek your gatherings, O Christ, and the pleasant places of your people,

lines.la: Concilia, Elysiosque agros: huc casta cruentis
lines.en: Assemblies, and the Elysian fields: hither chaste from bleeding

lines.la: Vina tuis ducunt, deprompto sanguine, venis.
lines.en: wines lead from your veins, with blood drawn forth.

lines.la: Dulcior ipsa mero, rosei mihi fluminis vnda
lines.en: Sweeter than unmixed wine itself to me is the wave of the rosy stream

lines.la: Christe tui: hi calices quem non fecere disertum?
lines.en: of yours, O Christ: whom have these chalices not made eloquent?

lines.la: Ite procul Bacchi fœdantia pocula mentes,
lines.en: Go far away, you cups of Bacchus that defile minds,

lines.la: Dummodo melliflui hæc hilarent me vina cruoris.
lines.en: provided that these wines of honey-flowing blood gladden me.

lines.la: AQVA LATERIS CHRISTI LAVA ME.
lines.en: WATER FROM THE SIDE OF CHRIST, WASH ME.

lines.la: Pure latex Christi lateris de vulnere manans,
lines.en: O pure liquid flowing from the wound of Christ's side,

lines.la: Lethiferæ labis de cordibus elue fæces,
lines.en: wash away the dregs of deadly stain from our hearts,

lines.la: Nulli etenim maculæ patet alti ianua Regis.
lines.en: for the door of the high King is open to no blemish.

printed_notes.text: Insinuatur hic virtutum inter se concatenatio.
printed_notes.text_en: Here the linking of virtues to one another is implied.
printed_notes.explanation: The clustered ornaments in the verse become an image of the virtues joined into a mutually supporting whole.

lines.la: Passio Christi FORTIFICA ME.
lines.en: PASSION OF CHRIST, STRENGTHEN ME.

lines.la: Cruda flagella, truces inflictæ cuspidis ictus,
lines.en: The cruel scourges, the fierce blows of the spear-point driven in,

lines.la: Christe, tuæ carni, toto cuî corpore nullum
lines.en: O Christ, to your flesh, on whose whole body no

lines.la: Verber inane datur, valido me robore firment.
lines.en: lash is dealt in vain, may they strengthen me with mighty strength.

lines.la: MORS CHRISTI VIVIFICA ME.
lines.en: DEATH OF CHRIST, GIVE ME LIFE.

lines.la: Mors tua, vita mihi, vt bello sit viuida virtus,
lines.en: Your death is life to me, that my courage may be lively in war,

lines.la: Vndique Cocyti dum circumfundimur armis;
lines.en: while we are surrounded on all sides by the arms of Cocytus;

lines.la: Nostra, Pater, molire tuas in pectora flammas,
lines.en: Father, hurl your flames into our breasts,

lines.la: Nos face, nos ferro, nos vulnere, victor, eodem
lines.en: us with the torch, us with the sword, us with the same wound, O victor,

lines.la: Confice, da sobolem caro comitem ire parenti.
lines.en: consume; grant that the offspring may go as a companion to the dear parent.

lines.la: Ibimus optato, duce te, data victima letho;
lines.en: We shall go to the desired death, with you as leader, a victim offered;

lines.la: Dummodo vitales tua mors mihi proferat orsus
lines.en: provided that your death brings forth life-giving beginnings for me.

lines.la: O BONE IESV EXAVDI ME.
lines.en: O GOOD JESUS, HEAR ME.

lines.la: O gregis alme tui custos, mitissime Iesu,
lines.en: O kindly guardian of your flock, most gentle Jesus,

lines.la: Summe ouium Pastor, cui sunt tot ouilia curæ,
lines.en: Supreme Shepherd of the sheep, to whom so many sheepfolds are a care,

lines.la: Quæ nunquam surda pietas tua præterit aure,
lines.en: which your loving-kindness never passes by with a deaf ear,

lines.la: Ne mitis renuas in voces ire precantum.
lines.en: do not, gentle one, refuse to heed the voices of those praying.

lines.la: INTRA VVLNERA TVA ABSCONDE ME.
lines.en: HIDE ME WITHIN YOUR WOUNDS.

lines.la: Vulneribus latuisse tuis sit facta potestas,
lines.en: Let the power be granted to have lain hidden in your wounds,

lines.la: Præsertim in roseo traiecti limine cordis,
lines.en: especially at the rosy threshold of the pierced heart,

lines.la: His etenim semper versabor tutus in oris,
lines.en: for in these shores I shall always dwell safe,

lines.la: Donec triste nefas lacrymarum fonte luatur.
lines.en: until the grievous wickedness is washed away and expiated by a fountain of tears.

lines.la: ET NOLI ME SEPARARE ABS TE, SED PONE ME IVXTA TE.
lines.en: AND DO NOT SEPARATE ME FROM YOU, BUT PLACE ME BESIDE YOU.

lines.la: Tanto sim tecum nexu constrictus amoris,
lines.en: May I be bound to you with so great a bond of love,

lines.la: Auelli vt nequeam patriis amplexibus vnquam,
lines.en: that I can never be torn away from your fatherly embraces,

lines.la: Quolibet aut casu, aut quouis discrimine rerum,
lines.en: either by any chance, or by any crisis of affairs,

lines.la: Dum mihi vita comes, dum spiritus hos reget artus,
lines.en: while life is my companion, while breath shall rule these limbs,

loci.virgil: dum memor ipse mei, dum spiritus hos regit artus.

lines.la: Ac tua me pietas maturum poscet Olympo.
lines.en: and your loving-kindness claims me, ripe for Olympus.

pages.cento: VT CVM ANGELIS, ET SANCTIS TVIS, &c.

lines.la: VT CVM ANGELIS, ET SANCTIS TVIS, &c.
lines.en: THAT WITH THE ANGELS, AND THY SAINTS, etc.

lines.la: Fas vbi sit demum mihi sceptra resumere regni.
lines.en: Where it may at last be lawful for me to resume the sceptre of the kingdom.

lines.la: Proque suis donis, sua reddere iura Tonanti,
lines.en: And in return for His gifts, to render His dues to the Thunderer,

lines.la: Aligerûm ritu, citharis fidibusque sonoris,
lines.en: In the manner of the winged ones, with lyres and sounding strings,

lines.la: Et vocum innumeris concentibus atria cæli
lines.en: And with the countless harmonies of voices, the halls of heaven

lines.la: Complere ac lætoster Io, ter dicere Pæan,
lines.en: To fill, and joyful to say thrice 'Io', thrice 'Paean',

lines.la: Insertosq́ue choris Superûm, tria Numinis ora
lines.en: And, joined to the choirs of the Ones Above, the three faces of the Godhead

lines.la: Cernere, lustratos diuini lumine vultus.
lines.en: To behold, faces illuminated by the light of the Divine.

lines.la: Felicem is sed enim censetur ducere vitam,
lines.en: But indeed he is deemed to lead a happy life,

lines.la: Qui mentem expleri nequit, ardescitque tuendo
lines.en: Who cannot satisfy his mind, and burns by gazing upon

loci.virgil: expleri mentem nequit ardescitque tuendo

lines.la: Id genus obtutus; stans hoc defixus in vno,
lines.en: A sight of that kind; standing fixed upon this one thing,

loci.virgil: dum stupet, obtutuque haeret defixus in uno,

lines.la: Quo datur æternùm cælesti sorte potiri.
lines.en: whereby it is granted to possess the heavenly lot forever.

pages.cento: MAGNIFICAT ANIMA MEA DOMINVM, ET EXVLTAVIT SPIRITVS MEVS, &c.

lines.la: MAGNIFICAT ANIMA MEA DOMINVM, ET EXVLTAVIT SPIRITVS MEVS, &c.
lines.en: MY SOUL MAGNIFIES THE LORD, AND MY SPIRIT HAS REJOICED, etc.

lines.la: Fas Superûm Regi grates persoluere dignas,
lines.en: It is right to pay worthy thanks to the King of Heaven,

loci.virgil: urbe, domo, socias, grates persolvere dignas

lines.la: Inque Deo exultare animis, pro munere tanto,
lines.en: and to exult in our souls in God, for so great a gift,

lines.la: Quo sua nos pietas dignatur, grata salutis
lines.en: with which His goodness deems us worthy, the pleasing of salvation

lines.la: Dona ferens, propriam sobolem cùm destinat aræ.
lines.en: bringing gifts, when He destines His own offspring for the altar.

lines.la: QVIA RESPEXIT HVMILITATEM ANCILLÆ SVÆ.
lines.en: BECAUSE HE HAS REGARDED THE HUMILITY OF HIS HANDMAID.

lines.la: Qui vilem famulæ sortem despectat ab alto,
lines.en: He who looks down from on high upon the lowly lot of His handmaid,

lines.la: Atque humiles habitare casas, vterique latebras
lines.en: and to dwell in humble cottages, and the hiding places of the womb

lines.la: Haudquaquam horrescit, nouus at fit sedibus hospes
lines.en: He does not shrink back at all, but becomes a new guest in these dwellings

lines.la: Virgineo partu, intemerato flore pudoris,
lines.en: by a virgin birth, with the undefiled flower of modesty,

lines.la: Me facere instituens diuina prole parentem,
lines.en: resolving to make me a parent by a divine offspring,

lines.la: Hinc Genitricis ego non munere fungor inani.
lines.en: hence I discharge no empty office of a Mother.

lines.la: ECCE ENIM EX HOC BEATAM ME DICENT OMNES GENERATIONES.
lines.en: FOR BEHOLD, FROM HENCEFORTH ALL GENERATIONS SHALL CALL ME BLESSED.

lines.la: Inde hominum omne genus me terq́ue quaterq́ue: [turnover line] beatam
lines.en: Thenceforth every race of men me three and four times blessed

lines.la: Esse feret, mihi dans æternum in sæcula nomen:
lines.en: shall declare to be, giving me an eternal name for all ages:

lines.la: In freta dum fluuij current, dum montibus vmbræ
lines.en: As long as rivers shall run into the seas, as long as shadows on the mountains

loci.virgil: In freta dum fluvii current, dum montibus umbrae

lines.la: Lustrabunt conuexa, polus dum sidera pascet,
lines.en: shall traverse the slopes, while the sky feeds the stars,

loci.virgil: lustrabunt convexa, polus dum sidera pascet,

lines.la: Semper honos, nomenq́; meum, laudesq; manebūt.
lines.en: forever shall my honor, and my name, and my praises remain.

loci.virgil: semper honos nomenque tuum laudesque manebunt,

lines.la: FECIT MIHI MAGNA QVI POTENS EST.
lines.en: HE WHO IS MIGHTY HAS DONE GREAT THINGS FOR ME.

lines.la: Tu das alme Pater (cui summa potentia rerum)
lines.en: You grant, O nurturing Father (who holds supreme power over the world),

lines.la: Sim magnæ Heroûm Isacidæ non infima stirpis
lines.en: that I may be not the lowest of the great Isaacid lineage of heroes,

lines.la: Gloria, virtutem vt non vnica pagina claudat
lines.en: glory, so that a single page may not confine my virtue.

lines.la: Certè magna nimis mutatæ est gratia sortis,
lines.en: Surely too great is the grace of my changed lot,

lines.la: Dum satis est famulæ, si laudis honoribus ornes
lines.en: while it is enough for your handmaid, if you adorn her with the honors of praise.

pages.cento: ET SANCTVM NOMEN EIVS, ET MISERICORDIA EIVS A PROGENIE, &c.

lines.la: ET SANCTVM NOMEN EIVS, ET MISERICORDIA EIVS A PROGENIE, &c.
lines.en: AND HOLY IS HIS NAME, AND HIS MERCY FROM GENERATION, etc.

lines.la: Iure tibi sanctum debetur Numine nomen,
lines.en: Rightly is a holy name owed to you by your divine power,

lines.la: Cùm tua, Rex, pietas sese diffundat in omnes.
lines.en: Since your mercy, O King, pours itself out upon all

lines.la: Insignes pietate viros, in quidquid vbique est
lines.en: men distinguished by piety, upon whatever there is everywhere

lines.la: sanctorum gentis, magnum quæ sparsa per orbem,
lines.en: of the race of saints, which is scattered through the great world,

loci.virgil: gentis Dardaniae, magnum quae sparsa per orbem.

lines.la: Quosque feret, tuleritq́ue ætas, queis mascula còrdi
lines.en: and those whom time shall bring, and has brought, in whose heart manly

lines.la: Insedit virtus, Domini quibus addidit alas
lines.en: virtue has settled, to whom the fear of the Lord has added wings,

lines.la: Ipse timor, spumantis equi calcaribus armos
lines.en: fear itself, the flanks of the foaming horse with spurs

lines.la: Dum sodit, atque asptos cogit decurrere calles.
lines.en: while it digs, and forces it to run down rough paths.

lines.la: FECIT POTENTIAM IN BRACHIO SVO, DISPERSIT SVPERBOS, &c.
lines.en: HE HATH SHOWED MIGHT IN HIS ARM, HE HATH SCATTERED THE PROUD, etc.

lines.la: Dextra potens Domini, magniq; ipsa agminis instar
lines.en: The mighty right hand of the Lord, itself like a great army,

lines.la: Dispergit tumido turgentia pectora fastu.
lines.en: scatters breasts swelling with turgid pride.

lines.la: Quam multi Libyco voluuntur marmore fluctus,
lines.en: As many as the waves that roll on the Libyan sea,

loci.virgil: quam multi Libyco volvuntur marmore fluctus

lines.la: Sæuus vbi Orion hybernis conditur yndis;
lines.en: where fierce Orion is hidden in the wintry waves;

lines.la: Vel quot sole nouo densæ torrentur aristæ,
lines.en: or as many as the thick ears of grain that are scorched by the early sun,

loci.virgil: vel cum sole novo densae torrentur aristae

lines.la: Aut Hermi campo, aut Lyciæ flauentibus aruis:
lines.en: either on the plain of Hermus, or in the yellowing fields of Lycia:

loci.virgil: aut Hermi campo aut Lyciae flaventibus arvis.

lines.la: Colla superborum tot fulua sternit arena,
lines.en: so many necks of the proud does it lay low on the tawny sand,

lines.la: Verè Marte potens supremi Numinis ira,
lines.en: the wrath of the supreme Godhead, truly mighty in war.

lines.la: Scuta sonent, pulsuque pedum tremat excita tellus,
lines.en: Let shields resound, and let the roused earth tremble with the beat of feet,

loci.virgil: Scuta sonant pulsuque pedum conterrita tellus.

lines.la: Aratæque micent peltæ, micet æreus ensis;
lines.en: and let bronze shields flash, let the brazen sword flash;

lines.la: Nequidquam in Superos insurgent arma tumentum.
lines.en: in vain will the arms of the swelling ones rise up against the Powers above.

lines.la: DEPOSVIT POTENTES DE SEDE, ET EXALTAVIT HVMILES.
lines.en: HE HATH PUT DOWN THE MIGHTY FROM THEIR SEAT, AND HATH EXALTED THE HUMBLE.

lines.la: Qui facit excelsas descendere montibus ornos,
lines.en: He who makes the lofty ash trees come down from the mountains,

loci.virgil: sub pedibus terram, et descendere montibus ornos.

lines.la: Non poterit regni sublimia sceptra tenentes,
lines.en: will he not be able to thrust those holding the sublime scepters of the kingdom,

lines.la: Illustri solio detrudere corde superbos?
lines.en: the proud in heart, down from their illustrious throne?

lines.la: summissos animo contrà, super æthera ferre?
lines.en: and on the other hand, to bear those lowly in spirit above the heavens?

pages.cento: ESVRIENTES IMPLEVIT BONIS, ET DIVITES DIMISIT INANES.

lines.la: ESVRIENTES IMPLEVIT BONIS, ET DIVITES DIMISIT INANES.
lines.en: HE HATH FILLED THE HUNGRY WITH GOOD THINGS, AND THE RICH HE HATH SENT EMPTY AWAY.

lines.la: Non potis esuriem vacuæ compescere mentis,
lines.en: Is he not able to curb the hunger of the empty mind,

lines.la: Vt sit adempia fames, & amor compressus habendi?
lines.en: so that hunger is taken away, and the love of possessing held in check?

lines.en: to great Abraham, and to his offspring and his descendants of old.

lines.la: GLORIA PATRI, ET FILIO, ET SPIRITVI SANCTO.
lines.en: GLORY BE TO THE FATHER, AND TO THE SON, AND TO THE HOLY SPIRIT.

lines.la: Mente sedet magno sua reddere iura Parenti,
lines.en: It is settled in the mind to render his due rights to the great Parent,

lines.la: Par simul est soboli, ob partos de morte triumphos,
lines.en: It is equally fitting for the Son, on account of the triumphs won over death,

lines.en: As much as lies in our power, to give the deserved honors of praise,

loci.virgil: non opis est nostrae, Dido, nec quicquid ubique est

lines.en: And also the Deity proceeding from both Deities,

lines.en: To celebrate in a similar manner, the will stands firm in the heart.

lines.la: Musa Maronis paraphrasticè canit Hymnum
lines.en: Maro's Muse sings the Hymn in paraphrase

lines.la: VENI CREATOR SPIRITVS, MENTES TVORVM VISITA.
lines.en: COME, CREATOR SPIRIT, VISIT THE MINDS OF YOUR PEOPLE.

lines.la: Spiritus alme veni, cælo demissus ab alto,
lines.en: Come, kindly Spirit, sent down from high heaven,

lines.la: Da nouus his nostris succedas sedibus hospes:
lines.en: Grant that you may enter these our dwellings as a new guest:

lines.la: Namque humiles habitare casas, & sordida rura,
lines.en: For to inhabit humble cottages, and unkempt countryside,

lines.la: Pauperis & tuguri congestum cespite culmen,
lines.en: And the roof of a poor hut heaped with turf,

lines.la: Numine magnus aues, præsepia grata Tonanti.
lines.en: You desire, great in divine power, mangers pleasing to the Thunderer.

lines.la: IMPLE SVPERNA GRATIA, QVÆ TV CREASTI PECTORA.
lines.en: FILL WITH HEAVENLY GRACE THE HEARTS WHICH YOU HAVE CREATED.

lines.la: Sit tuus iste labor, cæli Spirabile Numen:
lines.en: Let this be your task, Life-giving Deity of heaven:

lines.la: Inspirare animis, quos dextera flaminis auræ
lines.en: To breathe into the souls, which the right hand of the blowing breeze

lines.la: Condidit è nihilo, certantibus arma tuorum,
lines.en: Created out of nothing, the arms of your people for those striving,

lines.la: Dona & habere humeris, & vertice figere cristas,
lines.en: And to have gifts on their shoulders, and to fix crests on their head,

loci.virgil: donat habere umeris et vertice figere cristas.

lines.la: Gratiæ vti clypeo gestare insigne paternum.
lines.en: To use the shield of grace, to bear the paternal emblem.

lines.la: QVI PARACLETVS DICERIS.
lines.en: YOU WHO ARE CALLED THE PARACLETE.

lines.la: Tu potis es mœstos animi lenire dolores,
lines.en: You are able to soothe the sad sorrows of the mind,

lines.la: Solando verbis factisque auertere curas,
lines.en: By consoling with words and deeds to turn away cares,

lines.la: Mens pietate potens, longum seruata per æuum,
lines.en: A mind powerful in piety, preserved through a long age,

lines.la: Non ignara mali, miseris succurrere prompta.
lines.en: Not ignorant of evil, ready to help the wretched.

loci.virgil: Non ignara mali, miseris succurrere disco."

lines.la: DONVM DEI ALTISSIMI.
lines.en: THE GIFT OF THE MOST HIGH GOD.

lines.la: Tene vocem donum, ac rebus melioribus æquem?
lines.en: Shall I call you a gift, and equal you to better things?

lines.la: Non tibi par sceptrum, Iliene quod gesserat olim,
lines.en: Not equal to you is the scepter, which Ilione had once borne,

loci.virgil: praeterea sceptrum, Ilione quod gesserat olim,

lines.en: The eldest of Priam's daughters, and the necklace for the neck

loci.virgil: maxima natarum Priami, colloque monile

lines.la: Baccatum, aut duplex gemmis auroque corona;
lines.en: Set with pearls, or the double crown with gems and gold;

lines.la: Munus es immensum Patris omnipotentis Olympi.
lines.en: You are the immense gift of the omnipotent Father of Olympus.

lines.la: Munera nulla putem Iliacis erepta ruinis,
lines.en: I would consider as nothing the gifts snatched from the Trojan ruins,

loci.virgil: Munera praeterea, Iliacis erepta ruinis,

lines.en: The ornaments of Argive Helen, which she from Mycenae,

loci.virgil: Pergama cum peteret inconcessosque hymenaeos,

lines.en: All these things are nothing compared to the one gift of the Thunderer.

lines.la: FONS VIVVS, IGNIS, GHARITAS, ET SPIRITALIS VNCTIO.
lines.en: LIVING FOUNTAIN, FIRE, CHARITY, AND SPIRITUAL UNCTION.

lines.en: You are the fountain of living water, leaping into the lofty

lines.la: Caelicolum montes, vis ignea, flammeus ardor
lines.en: mountains of the heaven-dwellers, a fiery force, a flaming ardour

lines.en: of a mind kindled by the love of God; and a fragrant unction

lines.en: which brings back to you, sweating from the scented wood,

lines.en: balsams that surpass the berries of the ever-leafy acanthus

loci.virgil: balsamaque et bacas semper frondentis acanthi?

lines.en: by countless degrees: you, finally, the Godhead

lines.en: You continually adorn your offspring with the sevenfold gift

lines.en: the Royal Majesty has made common to the offspring.

lines.en: You are the finger of the Father's right hand, you duly the Thunderer's

lines.en: promise, enriching throats with the heavenly word.

loci.virgil: at sapor indicium faciet manifestus et ora

lines.la: INFIRMA NOSTRI CORPORIS VIRTVTE FIRMANS PERPETI.
lines.en: STRENGTHENING THE WEAKNESSES OF OUR BODY WITH ENDURING STRENGTH.

lines.en: Hearts may be restored, with the deadly stain remitted.

lines.en: GRANT THAT THROUGH YOU WE MAY KNOW THE FATHER, AND KNOW THE SON, AND BELIEVE IN YOU, THE SPIRIT OF BOTH, AT ALL TIMES.

lines.en: With you as guide, it is lawful to know the Father, and may the serene

lines.en: And let there be to the one flowing from both into the ages his own Godhead,

lines.en: Equal radiance, and grace, and splendor, equal summit of honor.

lines.en: Rich in wealth, may you also be the author of a generous gift to me.

lines.en: Bring hither the light inaccessible to the rays of the sun,

lines.en: Of the eternal Godhead, by which blind hearts may gleam.
